content_of_post_to_comment: “Half the harm that is done in this world is due to people who want to feel important. They don't mean to do harm; but the harm does not interest them. Or they do not see it, or they justify it because they are absorbed in the endless struggle to think well of themselves.” —T.S. Eliot, from The Cocktail Party Feels relevant.
comment: The interesting tension is that the desire to see ourselves as good can sometimes become a shield against seeing consequences. Perhaps humility begins not with thinking less of ourselves, but with staying curious about the harm our self-image hides.
